title: [bug] `TensorIterator` segfaults when inputs broadcast over output, and output is at least 2 dims larger than inputs.

labels.name: module: crash
labels.description: Problem manifests as a hard crash, as opposed to a RuntimeError

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

This one was originally observed in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/78867.
To reproduce, checkout https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/79201 and run

```python
import itertools
import torch

res = [torch.rand((5,) * d, dtype=torch.double, device='cpu') for d in range(4)]

for input in itertools.product(res, repeat=3):
    print(f"shape : {[i.shape for i in input]}")
    torch.foo(*input)

```

This outputs:
```
...
CPU kernel                                                                                                             
shape : [torch.Size([5, 5, 5]), torch.Size([]), torch.Size([])]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              CPU kernel                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   /home/nik/git/Quansight/pytorch/test.py:8: UserWarning: An output with one or more elements was resized since it had shape [5, 5, 5], which does not match the required output shape []. This behavior is deprecated, and in a future PyTorch release outputs will not be resized unless they have zero elements. You can explicitly reuse an out tensor t by resizing it, inplace, to zero elements with t.resize_(0). (Triggered internally at  /home/nik/git/Quansight/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/Resize.cpp:17.)      
  torch.foo(*input)                                                                                                    
shape : [torch.Size([5, 5, 5]), torch.Size([]), torch.Size([5])]                                                       
CPU kernel                                                                                                             
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

This also segfaults on CUDA, which might suggest that the issue is in the TI's internals.
NOTE, however, that the script works just fine if restricted to tensors with dim `< 3`.

A simpler repro with an `out` specified:
```python
In [1]: import torch

In [2]: x = torch.rand(2)

In [3]: y = torch.rand(())

In [4]: z = torch.rand(2, 2, 2)

In [5]: torch.add(x, y, out=z)
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
This indicates that, potentially, all out functions are unsafe.

Segfaults happen when `out` is at least 2 dimensions larger than any of the inputs in point-wise-like operations.

### Versions

master
